description: Sync people, cohorts, feature flags and annotations from the PostHog projects you select. Events are not synced.
opening: Sync people, cohorts, feature flags and annotations from the PostHog projects you select. Each person is one contact document built from their PostHog properties. Cohorts, feature flags and annotations are one document each, naming their creator.

PostHog permissions are not imported, so every synced item is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Events, such as pageviews and custom events, are not synced. People deleted in PostHog stay in HydraDB, and feature flags and annotations that PostHog marks deleted stay searchable.

connect.auth: PostHog uses a personal API key.

credentials.name: project_id
credentials.text: A PostHog project id. It is used when you select no projects. The projects you select take its place.

steps.title: Create a personal API key
steps.text: In PostHog, create a personal API key.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the key as `api_key` and a project id as `project_id`.

steps.title: Select projects
steps.text: HydraDB lists the projects of the organization the key belongs to, from `https://app.posthog.com`. The connection form has no setting for another PostHog address. Select the projects to sync. Each one syncs separately.

steps.title: Give each project its own collection
steps.text: If you select more than one project, send each to its own collection. Records of the same type with the same id in two projects can replace each other when they land in the same collection.

connect.account: One connector reads projects from one PostHog organization, the one the API key belongs to.

sync.first_sync: People are read in full, whatever the window. Cohorts, feature flags and annotations reach back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Every sync reads all people in each selected project again, which is slow for projects with many people. A cohort is picked up again when PostHog recalculates it. Feature flags and annotations are picked up again when they are updated.
sync.edits: An edited item replaces its document.
sync.deletes: Deleted people are not removed. A person deleted in PostHog stays searchable in HydraDB. Feature flags and annotations that PostHog marks deleted are still synced and searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.posthog_stream
shared_attributes.text: The record type: `persons`, `cohorts`, `feature_flags` or `annotations`. Limits a query to one type, for example only people. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: stream_type
shared_attributes.text: The record type, shown when you inspect the item. To limit a query by type, use `additional_metadata.posthog_stream`.

documents.name: People
documents.one_document: One person in a selected project.
documents.title: `PostHog persons: <name>`, using the person's name, else their first and last name, else their email. `PostHog persons` when there is none.
documents.text: Contact details taken from the person's properties, described below. Then notes with a `Name` line, a `Distinct IDs` line, and every person property that has a single value, in alphabetical order as `property: value`. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: display_name, first_name, last_name, email, emails
attributes.text: The person's name and email, from their properties. The email comes from `email` or `$email`. They identify the person in the graph.

attributes.name: provider_user_id
attributes.text: The person's first distinct id. It is part of the contact details and identifies the person in the graph.

attributes.name: linkedin_url, x_handle
attributes.text: Social handles, from `linkedin_url` or `linkedin`, and from `x_handle`, `twitter_handle` or `username`. The first one available identifies the person in the graph.

attributes.name: entity_type
attributes.text: Always `person`. It makes the contact a person in the graph.

attributes.name: owner, owner_email
attributes.text: The contact owner's name and email, from the person's properties. The graph records the owner as a separate person.

attributes.name: distinct_ids
attributes.text: All of the person's distinct ids, written as the `Distinct IDs` line. Only the first one identifies the person in the graph.

attributes.name: job_title, organization_name, organization_id, lifecycle_stage
attributes.text: Job, company and lifecycle stage, from matching properties or from `title`, `company`, `company_id` and `stage`.

attributes.name: phones
attributes.text: Phone numbers from the `phones`, `phone` and `phone_number` properties. They do not identify the person in the graph.

attributes.name: labels, tags, url
attributes.text: Labels, tags and a URL from the person's properties or record. The URL is part of the contact details and is not a link back.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the person was created. It is part of the contact details and sets the result date.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the person was last updated, when PostHog provides it. It does not set the result date.

attributes.name: Other person fields
attributes.text: Every other field of the person record, kept for inspection only.

documents.name: Cohorts
documents.title: `PostHog cohorts: <name>`.
documents.text: `Name`, `Description` and `Count` lines, with the creator as the author. The title is searchable too.
documents.files: None. The list of members is not synced.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.text: The creator's name, or their email when there is no name. It is written as the author, and the graph records the creator as the author.

attributes.name: created_by_email
attributes.text: The creator's email, attached to the author in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the cohort was created. Not searchable.

attributes.name: last_calculation
attributes.text: When PostHog last recalculated the cohort. A recalculation is what makes a sync pick the cohort up again.

attributes.name: Other cohort fields
attributes.text: Every other field of the cohort record, kept for inspection only.

documents.name: Feature flags
documents.title: `PostHog feature_flags` followed by the feature flag name. When a feature flag has no name, its key is not used in its place.
documents.text: `Name`, `Key`, `Active` and `Rollout percentage` lines, when present, with the creator as the author and the update time. The rollout percentage is the flag's top-level one. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.text: The creator's name, or their email when there is no name. It is written as the author, and the graph records the creator as the author.

attributes.name: created_by_email
attributes.text: The creator's email, attached to the author in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the flag was last updated, when PostHog provides it. It does not set the result date.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the flag was created. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Other flag fields
attributes.text: Other fields of the flag, including its targeting rules under `filters` and PostHog's `deleted` marker. Kept for inspection only, so targeting rules are not searchable.

documents.name: Annotations
documents.title: `PostHog annotations` followed by the first 80 characters of the content, with an ellipsis when it is longer. Just `PostHog annotations` when the content is empty.
documents.text: The annotation content, then `Insight`, `Scope` and `Date marker` lines, when present, with the creator as the author and the update time. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the annotation was last updated, or when it was created if PostHog gives no update time.

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.text: The creator's name, or their email when there is no name. It is written as the author, and the graph records the creator as the author.

attributes.name: created_by_email
attributes.text: The creator's email, attached to the author in the graph. Not searchable.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the annotation was last updated. It is part of the text and sets the result date.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the annotation was created. Sets the result date only when there is no update time. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Other annotation fields
attributes.text: Every other field of the annotation record, kept for inspection only.

example_searches: Which company and lifecycle stage does PostHog record for jane@acme.com?
What are the key, active status and rollout percentage of the new-checkout flag?
Which annotations were added around the March release?

connections: None. People, cohorts, feature flags and annotations are not linked to each other.
people: Each person, identified by their name, email, social handle and first distinct id.
A person's owner, as a separate person.
The creator of cohorts, feature flags and annotations, as their author.
graph.from_text: The text of people, cohorts, feature flags and annotations.

not_synced: Events, including pageviews, autocapture and custom events.
Insights, dashboards, session recordings, experiments and surveys.
Cohort members. A cohort carries its member count only.
Targeting rules of feature flags, in the searchable text.
Deletions: people deleted in PostHog stay in HydraDB.
